purpose: Accepted provisional DMC2 Mini profile and explicitly deferred integrations for the LinuxCNC-owned Mesa configuration

requirements.reason: The user accepted nominal 1000 pulses/mm for the rough safe-zone GUI. The caliper readings were explicitly eyeballed sanity checks; fine per-axis calibration remains later work.
These are the user-observed physical mappings used by every prior successful motion and home test.
The user accepted these conservative values derived from the published DMC2 Mini cutting region.
Each accepted switch point is exactly 250 pulses beyond the final normal maximum, preserving the confirmed final backoff.
The user accepted 30 mm/s as the provisional LinuxCNC motion ceiling.
The user accepted 50 mm/s^2 as the provisional LinuxCNC acceleration ceiling.

value.final_move: -0.25 mm at 0.25 mm/s (250 pulses at 250 pulses/s)

requirements.reason: LinuxCNC 2.9.10's same-sign switch sequence performs the fast approach, clears the switch, makes the slow positive latch pass, and makes the exact negative final move.

requirements.value: Momentary pyvcp.home-all output connected directly to halui.home-all
requirements.reason: The operator button invokes LinuxCNC's existing configured HOME_SEQUENCE 0/1/2 path for X then Y then Z; no second homing sequence or substituted motion values were introduced.

requirements.value: LinuxCNC incremental axis jog; continuous generated-count target replacement for same-axis/same-direction motion; exactly one overwriteable pending request for a stop/reversal
requirements.reason: Same-motion detents replace the target using only progress already generated by the Mesa count. Axis or direction changes stop first and overwrite one pending slot; idle packets never reconstruct dropped events.

The user requested independent multiplication of each existing pendant rate. The accepted 30 mm/s LinuxCNC machine ceiling, acceleration, pulse distance, and exact limit-bounce policy remain unchanged.

requirements.value: Odd/even snapshot generation brackets every bridge publication; the 1 kHz supervisor accepts only a stable even generation
requirements.reason: HAL pin writes are individual operations. The generation guard prevents a detent, selector, E-stop, and sequence value from different 20 ms reports being combined or consumed twice.

requirements.value: 7I95T DPLL timer 1 at -100 us; current-cycle hm2_eth packet-error selects command-matched feedback instead of stale FPGA feedback
requirements.reason: The active official 7i95t_1pktv2d firmware contains DPLL and StepGen v2. LinuxCNC's HostMot2 documentation recommends DPLL latching for Ethernet stepgens, and the installed hm2_eth manual specifically recommends command-matched feedback during a reported lost packet so stale generated-position data cannot cause a false following error.

requirements.value: Persistent and direct launch paths explicitly set LINUXCNC_FORCE_REALTIME=1; /usr/bin/rtapi_app is root:root mode 4755
requirements.reason: This Pi runs a PREEMPT_RT kernel but does not expose the legacy /sys/kernel/realtime flag required by LinuxCNC 2.9.10's automatic probe. Without the explicit environment setting, the servo thread silently ran SCHED_OTHER and produced multi-millisecond Mesa read delays.

requirements.value: Previously validated directional realtime jog stop; one -250 pulse jog at 1500 pulses/s; exact generated-count and raw-clear verification
requirements.reason: The matching own limit blocks only the toward direction and permits the negative bounce; either other limit blocks the active motor. Exactly one matching raw-and-latched limit at startup is attributed before LinuxCNC is enabled and receives the same exact bounce. Wrong-axis, multiple, otherwise unattributed, non-exact, uncleared, or timed-out events fail closed.

requirements.value: X+x10 -> X+x1 -> OFF -> CW -> CCW -> three complete side-button clicks
requirements.reason: Recovery remains input-only; the external E-stop gate stays false until the exact gesture completes, then LinuxCNC reset/on is requested.

requirements.value: Puck IN0 is connected to motion.probe-input plus motion.digital-in-00; the first explicitly approved moving test probes only Z at 0.1 mm/s from recorded X/Y and returns to machine Z home after contact; IN1 remains status-only
requirements.reason: The separate no-motion path remains available, while tool-height-first-test.ngc is the deliberately slow first live G38.2 validation and does not alter coordinates or the tool table.

requirements.value: M64/M65 P0 request OUT5 through a realtime program-running gate; motion.digital-in-01 reports the gate state; normal completion, timeout, and ON_ABORT_COMMAND clear the request
requirements.reason: The no-motion panel test has an exact 300-second maximum contact window. The moving first test enables OUT5 only after its operator gate and removes it before the Z-home return; the abort handler remains the fallback cleanup.

requirements.value: No alarm pin is consumed by this profile
requirements.reason: Alarm monitoring remains required future work; no input or polarity has been assigned.

requirements.value: No Mesa SSR is assigned; LinuxCNC controls only each internal stepgen enable
requirements.reason: The shared physical drive-enable wiring was not proven, so this profile does not command it.

requirements.value: LinuxCNC M3/M4/S/M5 is routed through a direction-aware realtime H100 sequencer and hm2_modbus on Mesa PktUART channel 1; 24000 RPM maps to verified DMC2 F004/F005 raw 4000 (400.0 Hz), with a 6000 RPM software minimum; startup writes STOP then zero, RUN waits for 0201H readback; the user-verified top-down installation mapping is H100 0001H=physical CCW and 0004H=physical CW, so standard mill M3 writes 0004H, M4 writes 0001H, and M5 writes STOP before clearing frequency
requirements.reason: On 2026-08-24 the stopped one-time write changed live F004/F005 from raw 500/500 to 4000/4000, and the restarted LinuxCNC profile read back observed=expected=4000, ready=true, block-code=0, STOP=8, commanded/output frequency=0, and VFD fault=0. No spindle RUN was sent during this verification.

requirements.value: Not run while constructing this configuration
requirements.reason: The first Mesa/Nano/LinuxCNC launch and every physical motion remain separate explicit hardware actions.
